what: Put a hand on the photo and it melts first into a cloud-pattern blotch (noise delay .6 + spread .4), then scatters at 1.45s into four layers of particles (far 1.25 · back 1 · middle .5 · front 0 depth, opacity .25·.3·.38·1) — bright areas become gold leaf (accent color), some dark areas turn white light, and the rest keep the photo color, drifting sideways like a school of small fish. Within 31.6px of the cursor (at 680 width) each layer reacts differently — front and far layers step aside leaving a hole (55% gather at the rim · 25% spread to .9~1.2R · 20% stay inside and swim, 10% of the front layer pushed a further .24~.34R), the middle layer flicks ring particles out to .55~.9R every 8px·.28s and returns them at .78s, and the back layer emits ripple rings spreading at 86px per second every 14px·.9s (16px push, fading over 2.6s). When the cursor stops, it refills over 2.6s starting after 80ms. On release it returns to the photo in 1.15s in the same blotch order (smoothstep)

options.heal: Time (ms) for displaced particles to fill back in after the cursor stops, default 2600
options.spread: Scatter distance (px, based on 680 width), default 78
options.radius: Radius the cursor pushes (px, at 680 width), default 31.625
options.gap: Particle spacing (px, based on width 680), default 3.2 — smaller is denser
options.[data-fx-part=image]: Photo (img) to scatter. If it isn’t an img (placeholder box), a water-surface pattern is drawn from that box’s background, text color, and accent color and scattered

note: WebGL1 point drawing. The original shader is not ported, it is rewritten to produce the same values (length, radius, layer, threshold) — the original samples a grid but here it is reduced to random position sampling (the cursor group split 55/25/20 is kept identical with a seed baked into each particle). The particle shader is drawn once transparently before the first touch to precompile. Touch toggles on and off with each press (does not block scrolling)
